newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed as dollar recovers.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed as dollar recovers.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed after the dollar recovered and key currencies retreated from gains set overnight.

June marks and Swiss franc futures ended not far from session lows, under pressure from dollar/mark strength in the face of mark/yen weakness. Marks and Swiss had posted strong gains overnight on more jawboning and followthrough from last week's dollar weakness, but they failed to hold their gains.
June marks slid through support at $0.5900 and Swiss erased $0.7000 support near midday and those levels were now seen as minor resistance, traders said.
"It was just a slow climb all around" in the dollar, one trader said. "We had a pretty strong move against the dollar and now things are calming down," he added.
Others said players were taking profits from recent currency gains.
June yen ended up strongly, but off from its nearly three-month overnight high as dollar/yen found its footing around 118.00 and firmed to just below 119.00.
"We got a nice turnaround in dollar/yen," one floor analyst said. "Coming off a seven-percent yen rally since Friday it was probably profit-taking," he said.
Traders said upside yen momentum could persist, but added the market may have come too far, too fast.
The floor analyst said the yen could see a short-term rally but said the long-term dollar bull trend was intact.
A futures trading floor manager, however, said yen bulls may be aiming for a run to 115.00 spot, or about $0.008740 in June yen.

"Just about anytime you get the cash below 120 it's pretty wide open as far as where it can go and that was evident overnight," he said. The dollar slid to 117.50 yen overnight. "The next cash level realistically is 115.00," he said.
He said a move back to 120.00, about $0.008376 in June yen, would find resistance.
He said perceptions continue that the interest rate differential between the U.S. and Japan may narrow.
Traders noted heavy fund activity during the session and said volume was brisk until early afternoon. It was moderate on the close, they said.
Yen traded an estimated 42,167 contracts Monday compared with 75,965 on Friday, marks traded 25,254 versus 42,335 Friday and Swiss volume was estimated at 21,318 against 53,744 on Friday.

At the close, June yen was up $0.000093 to $0.008431, marks fell $0.0068 to $0.5873, Swiss francs fell $0.0081 to $0.6974, sterling was up $0.0012 to $1.6224, Can dollar rose $0.0011 to $0.7215, Aus dollar rose $0.0002 to $0.7785, and Mex peso was up $0.000150 to $0.124550.
